questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The order of acidic strength of boron trihalides is
questions.solution: Boron trihalides are Lewis acids. The back bonding determines its acidic strength, more is the $\pi$-back bonding, less is the acidity. Thus, due to better overlapping of orbitals it promotes better $\pi$-back bonding, hence $\mathrm{BF}_3$ is least acidic in nature. Thus, order of acidic strength is $\mathrm{BF}_3 \lt  \mathrm{BCl}_3 \lt  \mathrm{BBr}_3 \lt  \mathrm{BI}_3$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Find the correct matches of the substances, given in Column I, from their characteristic properties given in Column II.
S.No.Column IS.No.Column II
WTlADecomposes steam to form its dioxide and dihydrogen gas.
X$CCl_4$BConsists of twenty 6-membered rings and twelve 5 membered rings.
YTinC+3 oxidation state is highly oxidising.
Z$C_{60}$DElectron precise species, neither acts as electron donor nor as electron acceptor.
questions.solution:
Thallium (Tl) belongs to Group 13. Due to the inert pair effect, the +1 oxidation state is more stable than the +3 oxidation state. Consequently, the +3 oxidation state of Tl is highly oxidising, which matches property C.

Carbon tetrachloride (CCl_{4}$) has a central carbon atom bonded to four chlorine atoms. It has a complete octet and no lone pairs, making it an electron-precise species that acts neither as an electron donor nor as an electron acceptor. This matches property D. \\ \\ Tin (Sn) reacts with steam at high temperatures to form tin dioxide (SnO_{2}$) and hydrogen gas (H_{2}$), represented by the reaction $\mathrm{Sn} + 2\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O} \rightarrow \mathrm{SnO}_{2} + 2\mathrm{H}_{2}$. This matches property A. \\ \\ Fullerene (C_{60}$) is a cage-like molecule consisting of twenty 6-membered rings and twelve 5-membered rings, which matches property B.

Therefore, the correct mapping is W=C, X=D, Y=A, Z=B.

Answer: $\mathrm{W}=\mathrm{C} \quad \mathrm{X}=\mathrm{D} \quad \mathrm{Y}=\mathrm{A} \quad \mathrm{Z}=\mathrm{B}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The order of acidic strength of boron trihalides is
questions.solution:
Boron trihalides are Lewis acids because the boron atom is electron-deficient, having only six electrons in its valence shell. The acidic strength depends on the extent of back-bonding between the lone pair of the halogen atom and the empty $2p$ orbital of the boron atom.

The back-bonding involves the overlap of the $2p$ orbital of boron with the $np$ orbital of the halogen. The extent of this overlap is maximum for $\mathrm{BF}_3$ because both boron and fluorine have $2p$ orbitals, leading to effective $p\pi-p\pi$ back-bonding. This reduces the electron deficiency of boron significantly.

As the size of the halogen increases from fluorine to iodine, the energy gap between the boron $2p$ orbital and the halogen $np$ orbital increases, and the overlap becomes less effective. Consequently, the extent of back-bonding decreases in the order $\mathrm{BF}_3 \gt \mathrm{BCl}_3 \gt \mathrm{BBr}_3 \gt \mathrm{BI}_3$.

Since back-bonding reduces the Lewis acidity, the acidic strength follows the reverse order: $\mathrm{BF}_3 \lt \mathrm{BCl}_3 \lt \mathrm{BBr}_3 \lt \mathrm{BI}_3$.

Answer: $\mathrm{BF}_3\lt \mathrm{BCl}_3\lt \mathrm{BBr}_3\lt \mathrm{BI}_3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The increasing order of atomic radii of the following group 13 elements is
questions.solution:
The group 13 elements are Boron (B), Aluminium (Al), Gallium (Ga), Indium (In), and Thallium (Tl).

Moving down the group, the atomic radius generally increases due to the addition of new electron shells.

However, there is an anomaly between Aluminium (Al) and Gallium (Ga). Gallium follows the 3d transition series, which contains electrons that provide poor shielding of the nuclear charge. This results in a higher effective nuclear charge for Gallium, causing its atomic radius to be slightly smaller than that of Aluminium.

The atomic radii values are approximately: Al (143 pm), Ga (135 pm), In (167 pm), and Tl (170 pm).

Therefore, the increasing order of atomic radii is $\mathrm{Ga} \lt \mathrm{Al} \lt \mathrm{In} \lt \mathrm{Tl}$.

Answer: $\mathrm{Ga} \lt \mathrm{Al} \lt \mathrm{In} \lt \mathrm{Tl}$

questions.solution: When, Si (having 4 valence electrons) is doped with As (having 5 valence electrons), 4 electrons form covalent bonds, while the fifth electron remains free and increase conductivity. Hence, Si doped with As is $n$-type semiconductor.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Zeolites are shape selective structures because of
questions.solution: The reactions taking place in zeolites depend upon the size and shape of the reactant and product molecules and upon the pores and cavities of the zeolities. Hence, they are shape-selective catalyst.
